title: Finiteness of a morphism is local on the target
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. The following are equivalent: (1) $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; (2) there is a covering $S=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ by affine opens [def-weil-affine-spectrum] such that each $f^{-1}(U_j)$ is affine and the ring map $\mathcal O_S(U_j)\to\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(U_j))$ induced by $f$ is finite (makes $\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(U_j))$ a finitely generated $\mathcal O_S(U_j)$-module); (3) there is a covering $S=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ by opens such that each restriction $f^{-1}(U_j)\to U_j$ is finite. Moreover, if $f$ is finite, then for every open subscheme $U\subseteq S$ the restriction $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite (Stacks Morphisms, Lemma 01WI).

source.place: Lemma Tag 01WI (lemma-finite-local, line 11001); its proof: 'See Algebra, Lemma lemma-integral-local. Some details omitted.'
